name: C. SHANNON BACON
description: Concurred, argued that the Court of Appeals correctly applied the South Springs abandonment test and that Intrepid's actions demonstrated abandonment of most of its water rights, as speculation is inconsistent with beneficial use.

name: C. SHANNON BACON
description: Concurred, argued that the affidavit was sufficient to establish probable cause for the search warrant based on the CI's first-hand observations of methamphetamine, clarifying that while the Court of Appeals misread Belknap and overstated the sufficiency of first-hand observation, these errors were not fatal to the correct analysis.

name: MICHAEL E. VIGIL
description: Dissented, argued that the affidavit failed to provide sufficient factual detail to establish probable cause for trafficking, as it merely stated a conclusion without supporting facts, and that the majority's holding undermines New Mexico's constitutional protections for search warrants.

name: BRIANA H. ZAMORA
description: Concurred, argued that judicial immunity is available to public bodies under the CRA, but the Court of Appeals erred in finding NMRC immune without sufficient factual inquiry into the nature of the proceedings and conduct.

name: DAVID K. THOMSON
description: Concurred, argued that Stewart is entitled to legislative immunity for reassigning Candelaria's office and seat, as these are legitimate legislative activities, and her motives are irrelevant.

name: DAVID K. THOMSON
description: Concurred, delivering the majority opinion that the contempt fine payable to a third party is permitted under the judiciary's inherent contempt power and is constitutional.

name: C. SHANNON BACON
description: Concurred, argued that the emergency orders for gun violence and drug abuse are consistent with the PHERA and police power, and do not violate separation-of-powers principles, except for the suspension of the JDAI program which exceeded police power.

name: MICHAEL E. VIGIL
description: Dissented, argued that the majority's interpretation of "public health emergency" in PHERA is flawed because it removes the "emergency" context, allowing the Governor to assume sweeping emergency powers for any reason, and sets the bar too low for exercising extraordinary powers.

name: BRIANA H. ZAMORA
description: Dissented, argued that the PHERA limits executive action to genuine emergencies, and the Governor's orders for gun violence and drug abuse are not true emergencies under PHERA. Also argued that the majority's interpretation confers unlimited emergency powers to the Governor, raising constitutional concerns under the separation of powers doctrine.

name: DAVID K. THOMSON, CHIEF JUSTICE
description: Concurred, arguing that public schools are public accommodations under the NMHRA, thereby subjecting them to anti-discrimination laws and overruling prior inconsistent precedent.

name: DAVID K. THOMSON, Chief Justice
description: Concurred, argued that district courts have inherent authority to sua sponte raise suppression issues to protect fundamental rights, do not violate separation of powers, and do not inherently demonstrate bias.

name: BRIANA H. ZAMORA, Justice
description: Dissented, argued that while district courts have inherent authority to protect fundamental rights, the specific actions of the district court in this case constituted an abuse of discretion and created an appearance of bias by straying from its role as a neutral arbiter.

name: DAVID K. THOMSON
description: Concurred, argued that the Attorney General has the practical ability and implied authority to obtain and produce discovery materials from non-party executive agencies in state-interest civil litigation, and that the State's arguments regarding separation of powers and lack of control are unconvincing.

name: C. SHANNON BACON
description: Concurred, argued that the local ordinances are preempted by state law, including the Health Care Freedom Act, Medical Practice Act, Medical Malpractice Act, Health Care Code, and Uniform Licensing Act, and therefore must be invalidated.

name: JANE B. YOHALEM
description: Concurred, argued that the Act's provisions treating secondary mental impairments differently from secondary physical impairments violate the Equal Protection Clause of the New Mexico Constitution.

name: JULIE J. VARGAS
description: Concurred, argued that the authority to appropriate federal COVID-19 relief funds lies with the Legislature, not the Executive, based on the broad discretion given to states for these funds and the state constitution's appropriation clause.

name: DAVID K. THOMSON, JUSTICE
description: Concurred, argued that a district court judge has no authority at a preliminary examination to decide whether evidence was obtained from an unconstitutional search or seizure, as preliminary hearings are not the appropriate stage for such complex suppression issues.

name: BRETT R. LOVELESS, Judge Sitting by designation
MICHAEL E. VIGIL, Justice
description: Dissented, argued that the majority's conclusion contradicts basic principles of the New Mexico Constitution and fails to protect the accused's constitutional rights by preventing judges from considering the constitutionality of evidence at preliminary examinations.

name: C. SHANNON BACON, Chief Justice
description: Concurred, argued that partisan gerrymandering claims are justiciable under the New Mexico Constitution's Equal Protection Clause, adopting a three-part test to identify egregious gerrymandering that dilutes individual votes and undermines democratic principles.

name: MICHAEL E. VIGIL, Justice
description: Concurred, argued that the amendment did not violate the single-measure rule or have a misleading ballot title, and the petition for writ of mandamus was denied.

name: JULIE J. VARGAS
description: Concurred, argued that the informant's tip lacked a reliable factual basis and the agents' surveillance did not establish reasonable suspicion, making the defendant's seizure unreasonable under the New Mexico Constitution.

name: DAVID K. THOMSON
description: Concurred, argued that New Mexico's groundwater forfeiture statute allows for partial forfeiture, as mandated by the constitutional doctrine of beneficial use, which requires continuous use for water rights.

name: MICHAEL E. VIGIL
description: Concurred, argued that the public's right to recreate and fish in public water includes the right to touch privately owned beds below those waters.

name: MICHAEL E. VIGIL
description: Concurred, argued that the State failed to meet its burden of proving by clear and convincing evidence that no release conditions would reasonably protect the safety of the community, and that the nature of the offense alone is not sufficient for pretrial detention.

name: VIGIL, Chief Justice
description: Concurred, argued that judicial conduct can bar retrial under the New Mexico Constitution's double jeopardy clause and that the judge's conduct in this case met the Breit test criteria, thus barring the defendant's retrial.

name: VIGIL, Chief Justice
description: Concurred, argued that the arrest was unconstitutional under Article II, Section 10 of the New Mexico Constitution, requiring suppression of evidence.

name: DAVID K. THOMSON
description: Concurred, argued that the ETA is constitutional, the Commission's final order is reasonable and supported by evidence, and rejected all of New Energy's constitutional challenges and claims of error.

name: BACON, Justice
description: Concurred, argued that public health orders are a reasonable exercise of police power and do not constitute a regulatory taking requiring compensation.

name: THOMSON, Justice
description: Concurred, argued that summary judgment was improper due to disputed material facts regarding whether precondemnation activity constituted substantial interference and whether lost lease value is a compensable damage.

name: JUDITH K. NAKAMURA, Justice, Retired Sitting by designation
STEVEN BLANKINSHIP, Judge Sitting by designation
NAKAMURA, Justice
description: Concurred, arguing that the executive branch is authorized to impose business restrictions during a pandemic and that the temporary closure of indoor dining was not arbitrary or capricious.

name: DAVID K. THOMSON, Justice
description: Concurred, arguing that while the executive's actions were a proper exercise of emergency authority, broad and vague statutes granting such powers may pose long-term consequences to checks and balances, and judicial deference should wane as a crisis continues.
